create-menu.description: Creates a menu for the venue or replaces the existing one.

schema.description: Menu object describes venue's menu on Wolt.

currency.description: Primary currency of the menu. Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.

primary_language.description: Primary language of the menu. Two-letter ISO 639-1 language codes.

categories.description: Categories of items available in the menu.

items.description: Category for venue items.

subcategories.description:
Subcategories available for the category. This functionality is only available for retailers. 

If category has items, it cannot have subcategories too.

items.description: Items available in the subcategory.

examples: Hamburger with fried chicken patty, lettuce and tomato

image_url.description:
URL of the item’s image.

Aspect ratio must be 16:9 and image type must be jpeg with a white background.
Recommended size is 1000 x 562.5.

price.description: The price of the item as it appears to the consumer. The price includes any taxes.

sales_tax_percentage.description:
Tax percentage of the item. The price includes any taxes. 
If a non-null, yet invalid, tax rate is provided, while ‘price’ is set to 0,
Wolt will automatically apply the highest valid tax rate for that country,
to avoid future VAT compliance issues, in case of a price change.

alcohol_percentage.description: Alcohol content percentage of the item.

serving_size.description: Unit of measure for caffeine content in the item.

value.description: Amount of caffeine content in the item. For example, 0.5mg will be 0.5.

weekly_availability.description: Weekly availability time spans for the item.

opening_day.description: Day of the week the category becomes available for sale.

opening_time.description: Hour of the opening day at which the category becomes available for sale.

closing_day.description: Day of the week the category becomes not available for sale.

closing_time.description: Hour of the closing day at which the item becomes not available for sale.

weekly_visibility.description: Weekly visibility for this item. It is used to see whether an item being sold by a venue even if it’s not available at the moment.

opening_day.description: Day of the week the category becomes available for sale.

opening_time.description: Hour of the opening day at which the category becomes available for sale.

closing_day.description: Day of the week the category becomes not available for sale.

closing_time.description: Hour of the closing day at which the item becomes not available for sale.

enabled.description: Indicates whether item is available for sale or not. When `false` the item will not be visible to consumers.

discounted.description: Indicates whether the item is at discount and provide the original price of item along with discount type.

original_price.description: Original price of the item on which discount was applied.

disabled_until.description:
Date and time when the item will be available for sale again.

This field is used to mark an item as temporarily unavailable for sale. If this field is set, then the `enabled` property value is ignored.

delivery_methods.description:
Each item has delivery method availability.

- `takeaway`: An order with this item can be picked up by the consumer from the restaurant or store.
- `homedelivery`: An order with this item can be delivered by a Wolt courier.
- `eatin`: The order can be eaten in the restaurant. This feature has been deprecated at Wolt, so while this delivery method will appear in the menu, it is not supported for consumers.

items.description: Delivery method.

options.description:
Options available for the item.

NOTE: "nesting" options is possible using "sub_options"; the object "sub_option_values" (from a previous version of this API) is not recommended and in any case can't be used together with "sub_options" (validation will fail such payloads).

type.description: Option type. Options can be single or multi-choice. Single-choice options allow only one value to be selected. Multi-choice options allow more than one value to be selected.

selection_range.description: Maximum and minimum number of values that can be selected within this option (only supported for type: MultiChoice; see examples in fields' description).

max.description: Maximum number of values that can be selected in this multi choice option (eg - a Pizza can have a max of 5 toppings total).

min.description: Minimum number of values that must be selected in this multi choice option (eg - a Pizza that must have at least 1 topping, or a drink selection for a Burger meal).

max_same_selections.description: How many of the same value can be chosen in this option (eg - adding the same topping to the Pizza more than 2 times is not possible).

max_free_selections.description: How many selections of values can be made free of charge (eg all Pizza toppings cost an extra fee, but first 2 are free).

external_data.description: External data for mapping. Also known as "POS ID". Used to identify items on the venue's POS.

values.description: Options values that can be selected as part of the option.

selection_range.description:
Maximum and minimum number of option values that can be selected.

This field is required for `MultiChoice` type option.

max.description: Maximum number of option values that can be selected as part of the multi-choice selection.

min.description: Minimum number of sub-options that can be selected as part of the multi-choice selection.

price.description: The price of the item as it appears to the consumer, including taxes.

enabled.description: Indicates whether option value is available for sale or not. When `false` the item will not be visible to consumers.

default.description:
Default value for option values.

If there are multiple values marked as default then first one is picked.

external_data.description: External data for mapping. Also known as "POS ID". Used to identify items on the venue's POS.

sub_options.description:
Options to be "nested" (hidden) and presented only when this value is chosen; used for complex items, where the some modifier groups should only be visible based on previous selections.

NOTE: up to 3 sub-options can be created per value, each sub-option inherits all functionality of an "option", including the option to further nest sub-options to its "values", up to 3 times total.

regulatory_information.description: Regulatory information. Required for Uzbekistan venues.

name.description:
Name of the regulatory information field.
"ikpu_code" and "package_code" fields are required for Uzbekistan venues.

value.description: Value of the regulatory information field.

weight_in_g.description: Weight of the item in grams. This fields represents the amount per package.

volume_in_ml.description: Volume of the item in milliliters. This fields represents the amount per package.

quantity.description: Quantity of the item. This fields represents the amount per package.

display_unit.description:
A unit of measure for the item. Allowed values: `units`, `weight`, `volume`, `weight_100g`, `volume_100ml`.

If one of the fields for the amount per package: `weight_in_g`, `quantity`, or `volume_in_ml` --- is set then this field is mandatory. 
Its value _must_ correspond to the amount per package which is set, i.e, `volume` or `volume_100ml` for `volume_in_ml`, 
`weight` or `weight_100g` for `weight_in_g`, and `units` for `quantity`. Only one of the amount per package fields can be set at a time.

gtin_barcode.description: GTIN code of the item. Must be a valid GTIN-13 code.

merchant_sku.description: Merchant's own SKU for the item.

price.description: The price of the item as it appears to the consumer, including taxes.

vat_percentage.description: VAT percentage for the deposit. Typically the same as the VAT percentage of the item being sold.

VAT percentage for this add-on (used explicitly when the add-on has its own 'price'). 
For item modifiers (eg extra cheese) it's typically the same as the VAT percentage of the item being sold.
For distinct additional items (eg beverages in a meal) it's based on that additional item's VAT percentage

If a non-null, yet invalid, tax rate is provided, while ‘price’ is set to 0,
Wolt will automatically apply the highest valid tax rate for that country,
to avoid future VAT compliance issues, in case of a price change.

delivery_methods.description:
Each item has delivery method availability.

- `takeaway`: An order with this item can be picked up by the consumer from the restaurant or store.
- `homedelivery`: An order with this item can be delivered by a Wolt courier.
- `eatin`: The order can be eaten in the restaurant. This feature has been deprecated at Wolt, so while this delivery method will appear in the menu, it is not supported for consumers.

options.description:
Options available for the item.

NOTE: "nesting" options is possible using "sub_options"; the object "sub_option_values" (from a previous version of this API) is not recommended and in any case can't be used together with "sub_options" (validation will fail such payloads).

type.description: Option type. Options can be single or multi-choice. Single-choice options allow only one value to be selected. Multi-choice options allow more than one value to be selected.

selection_range.description: Maximum and minimum number of values that can be selected within this option (only supported for type: MultiChoice; see examples in fields' description).

max.description: Maximum number of values that can be selected in this multi choice option (eg - a Pizza can have a max of 5 toppings total).

min.description: Minimum number of values that must be selected in this multi choice option (eg - a Pizza that must have at least 1 topping, or a drink selection for a Burger meal).

max_same_selections.description: How many of the same value can be chosen in this option (eg - adding the same topping to the Pizza more than 2 times is not possible).

max_free_selections.description: How many selections of values can be made free of charge (eg all Pizza toppings cost an extra fee, but first 2 are free).

Maximum and minimum number of option values that can be selected.

This field is required for `MultiChoice` type option.

max.description: Maximum number of option values that can be selected as part of the multi-choice selection.

min.description: Minimum number of sub-options that can be selected as part of the multi-choice selection.

price.description: The price of the item as it appears to the consumer, including taxes.

enabled.description: Indicates whether option value is available for sale or not. When `false` the item will not be visible to consumers.

default.description:
Default value for option values.

If there are multiple values marked as default then first one is picked.

Retrieves the menu information for a specific venue. 

The response includes a `resource_url` that can be used to poll for the actual menu details.
The `resource_url` returns a `GetMenuResponse` object with `request_id`, `status`, optional `error`, and optional `menu`.

update-items.description:
Allows bulk updating item data such as price and visibility. This saves time and effort as venues can update their menus on the POS or menu management system and the changes will be reflected on the Wolt app.

Matching items between Wolt's menu and your system can be done with `sku`, `gtin` or `external_id`. When a match is found, the item is updated with the data provided in the payload.

data.description:
Items to update.

You must define exactly one of `external_id`, `gtin` or `sku` for each item to update.

external_id.description:
Unique identifier (POS ID or other external ID) for the item to update.

For venues with a full assortment integration, this identifier value should be the `listing_id` value used in the assortment file.

gtin.description:
Unique identifier (global trade item number) for the item to update.

For venues with a full assortment integration, this identifier is NOT supported in this API; to send partial updates with this API, we recommend leveraging the `sku` field.

sku.description:
Unique identifier (stock keeping unit) for the item to update.

For venues with a full assortment integration, this identifier is supported, and should be the same value used for `sku` in the assortment file.

price.description:
Price of the item presented in whole numbers in the lowest denomination, commonly cents. For example 10.00€ would be 1000.

For venues with a full assortment integration, updates of this field is supported (with usage of either `external_id` or `sku` as the identifier - see details above).

discounted_price.description:
Discounted price of the item presented in whole numbers in the lowest denomination, commonly cents. For example 10.00€ would be 1000.

If this field has a value then `price` field is mandatory.

For venues with a full assortment integration, updates of this field is supported (with usage of either `external_id` or `sku` as the identifier - see details above).

vat_percentage.description:
VAT percentage of the item. For example, 13.5 means 13.50%.
Note: even though this is technically not a required field, it should be sent for all items to avoid rely on the default values Wolt will apply if it's null (or not sent).

For venues with a full assortment integration, updates of this field is NOT supported.

enabled.description:
Controls whether the item is shown to consumers when they browse the venue's items.

For venues with a full assortment integration, updates of this field is supported (with usage of either `external_id` or `sku` as the identifier - see details above).

disabled_until.description:
Date and time when the item will be available for sale again.

This field is used to mark an item as temporarily unavailable for sale.

For venues with a full assortment integration, updates of this field is NOT supported.

in_stock.description:
Controls whether the item is shown out of stock to consumers.

This field should only be used for retail stores. Restaurant users can only disable out of stock items using the `enabled` field.

For venues with a full assortment integration, updates of this field is supported (with usage of either `external_id` or `sku` as the identifier - see details above).

update-item-inventory.description:
Allows venues to bulk update inventory quantities for items listed on Wolt. This saves time and effort as venues do not need to worry about receiving orders with out of stock items in them.

Integrating using this endpoint improves the consumer experience, preventing them from ordering unavailable items. If an item is out of stock, the venue can indicate that the item is out of stock by marking it "sold out" instead of removing the item from the menu.

Matching items between Wolt's menu and your system can be done with `sku`, `gtin` or `external_id`. When a match is found, the item is updated with the data provided in the payload.

get-venue-status.description:
Retrieve venue status by ID.

Returns various key status metrics for a venue, such as offline status, delivery radius and integration status.

The metrics also include status of the latest 3 orders - if the latest 3 orders are rejected, you can view it as a red flag and take remedial action.

closing_date.description: Calendar date on which the special schedule ends.

closing_time.description:
Time (24-hour clock, HH:mm) on **closing_date** when the venue closes.

The manually set estimated preparation time for the venue.

When using auto-accept, we prioritize the longer of two times: the preparation time you've set or the courier's expected arrival time. This way we ensure the venue has ample time to prepare the food even if we don't receive any adjusted preparation time during the auto-accept process.

update-venue-online-status.description:
Update venue's online status

To schedule the venue to be offline until a certain time, set `status=OFFLINE` and `until` to the desired date and time. Otherwise, the venue will be put offline indefinitely.

Scheduling for online status is not supported yet.

until.description:

update-venue-special-opening-times.description:
Sets the venue’s Special Opening times; These date-defined periods are overrides to your weekly schedule of opening hours. These allow to set opening and closing times in advance for specific events without changing the recurring schedule of your venue. For dates not specified in a request - regular opening hours will be used. Important to note:

- Each request must include the full list of future special opening and closing times. Any times not included in the new request will be removed, and the provided times will replace the previous ones.
- Dates can appear either in “days_closed” or “days_open” - not in both.
- Each “daily_availability” must have at least one entry (a pair of “open_time” and “close_time”); to apply more than one opening timeframe per specific entry of dates (or one date) - add each availability period as a pair of “open_time” and “close_time” within the “daily_availability” array. Those entries can’t overlap.

Times are interpreted in the **venue’s local time zone**.

It sends the courier's location to Wolt's system so that the user can track the courier in real time.
Updates the courier's location, heading (optional), and a flag indicating whether the courier is delivering the this order (optional, defaults to true).

This endpoint is only for Self Delivery. Location can only be updated after this order has been marked ready. Updating earlier is a bad request.

delivery-eta-update.summary: Send estimated time of arrival of the order (Self Delivery only)

It sends the estimated time of arrival (ETA) of the order to Wolt's system in minutes.

This endpoint is available only for Self Delivery orders.

accept-self-delivery-order.description: Accepts the self-delivery order and changes status of order to production.

If not provided, the venue's default order preparation and order delivery time will be used instead.

item_changes.description: Changes done to items in order during picking progress.

items.description: Replacement for an item in the order.

row_number.description:
Position of the item in the order. The row number is available in the get order response for reference.

The value must not repeat in the request.

replacement_items.description: Replacements for the item. For example substituting item with another, changes to weight or items missing.

replacement_type.description:
The type of replacement that was made - items can be missing, substituted, or could have different weights than originally ordered.

  - `count-change-replacement`: Items missing.
  - `menu-item-replacement`: Item was substituted with another one.
  - `weight-change-replacement`: Item's weight is different from what was ordered by the consumer.
  - `adhoc-replacement`: Item was substituted with another one due to unexpected issues.
  - `reduced-price`: Item’s price was reduced due to a promotion in the store, after purchase was made (eg loyalty plan pricing etc). `name` is optional — if omitted, it is resolved from the `barcode`.

barcode.description:
Barcode of the item.

- Required for `menu-item-replacement`.
- Required for `reduced-price` when `name` is omitted (used to resolve the item name).
- Optional for other replacement types.

count.description:
Number of items picked.

For example if an item is missing and it can't be substituted then 0 is count that is being picked.

name.description:
Name of the item as it should appear on the consumer's receipt.

- Required for `adhoc-replacement` (item not in menu, no barcode lookup possible).
- Optional for `reduced-price`: if omitted, the name is resolved from the barcode.
- Optional for `menu-item-replacement`: if omitted, the name is resolved from the barcode.

price.description:
The item price to use.

- For `menu-item-replacement` and `adhoc-replacement`: price of the substitute item.
- For `reduced-price`: the new reduced price of the original item.

amount.description: Price presented in whole numbers in the lowest denomination, commonly cents. For example 10.00€ would be 1000.

purchase_item_id.description: Unique identifier for the item in the purchase.

weight.description:
Actual weight picked in grams for the **same item** (weight adjustment).

**Applicable to:**
- `weight-change-replacement`: Adjust weight of the same item

Use this when the ordered item's weight differs from what was picked (e.g., ordered 1kg, only 500g available).
This is different from `picked_weight` which is used when substituting with a different weighted item.

picked_weight.description:
Actual weight picked in grams for weighted item **substitutions**.

**Applicable to:**
- `menu-item-replacement`: Substitute with a weighted menu item
- `adhoc-replacement`: Substitute with a weighted non-menu item

Use this when **substituting** an item with a weighted item.
This is different from `weight` which adjusts the weight of the same item.

Requires `weighted_item_input_type` to be specified.

weighted_item_input_type.description:
Specifies how to interpret the `picked_weight` value in relation to the `count` field for weighted substitutions.

**Note:** `picked_weight` always represents the actual picked weight in grams, regardless of this type.

**Applicable to:**
- `menu-item-replacement`: Substitute with a weighted menu item
- `adhoc-replacement`: Substitute with a weighted non-menu item

**Values:**
- `grams`: The `picked_weight` is the total weight in grams. Typically used with `count: 1`.
- `number_of_items`: The `picked_weight` is the total weight in grams for all items. The `count` field specifies the number of weighted units (e.g., count: 2 with picked_weight: 1000 means 2 items totaling 1000g).

Required when `picked_weight` is provided.

items.description:
**AVAILABLE UPON REQUEST ONLY**

Add a free or promotional item to the order without replacing existing items. Free items are always added at price 0.

**Item identification:** Items can be identified in two ways (following the same pattern as `replacement_items`):
- **Menu item (by barcode):** Provide `barcode` only. PIS will look up the item in the venue's menu
  and automatically enrich with the item ID before forwarding to RAPI.
- **Adhoc item (by name):** Provide `name` (no barcode). The item will be added as a custom item
  not from the menu, with price set to 0.

**Use cases:**
- Adding promotional or free items from the venue's menu
- Adding custom compensation items
- Adding free items related to specific order line items (use `row_number` to link)

{% callout variant="warning" %}
Contact Wolt support to request access.
{% /callout %}

barcode.description:
Barcode/GTIN of the menu item to add (for menu items).

When provided, PIS will look up the item in the venue's menu by barcode and automatically
enrich the request with the item ID before forwarding to RAPI.

If the barcode is not found in the menu, the request will fail with an error.

**Menu item addition:** Use this field alone (without `name`).
**Adhoc addition:** Leave this field null and provide `name` instead.

name.description:
Item name for adhoc (non-menu) additions.

Required when `barcode` is null. Ignored when `barcode` is provided.

**Adhoc addition:** Use this field (without `barcode`).

row_number.description:
Optional reference to an existing order item's row number.

Use this to indicate that the free item is related to a specific order line item.
This helps operations tools show why the item was added as free (e.g., "free drink
with meal from row 0").

The row number is available in the get order response for reference.

refund-items.description:
Refund a user for specific item(s) price, fully or partially, due to an unnecessary overcharge, an ad-hoc discount, or an item-specific quality issue.

Note: refunding to the payment method is possible only in non-cash orders, and only after an invoice is generated.

ℹ️ **The endpoint must be enabled by Wolt before it can be used. You can enable it by contacting your Wolt account or technical account manager**.

  - `QUALITY_ISSUES`: order or item related quality problems, etc.

Type of refund action to perform:
  - `REFUND_MONEY`: refund to the user’s payment method (only possible for non-cash orders)
  - `REFUND_CREDITS`: refund to the user’s Wolt account as credits (this must be used for cash orders)

refund-basket.summary: Create a refund to the purchase total ("basket-level")
refund-basket.description:
Refund a user for any basket-level issue, such as a basket discount, non-mappable item discounts, any order quality issue etc.

Note: Basket refunds are only possible as Wolt credits, due to tax allocation needs. Currently, a single basket refund per payload is allowed in a request.

ℹ️ **The endpoint must be enabled by Wolt before it can be used. You can enable it by contacting your Wolt account or technical account manager**.

schema.description:
This is a **venueless** endpoint to request a delivery fee estimate.

Like shipment promise endpoint, the delivery fee endpoint is used to check availability of Wolt for a given time, determine the estimated price and delivery time. However as a venueless endpoint, delivery fee endpoint can be used without any predetermined venue address.

Note that the endpoint cannot be used for address input validation. If the address does not exist, the endpoint will form a "best guess" of the location and resolve delivery availability using that address.

See [endpoint documentation](/docs/wolt-drive#venueless-endpoints) for more information.

schema.description: Order object describes an order on Wolt.

venue.description: Details of the venue where the order was placed.

price.description: Total price of the order.

amount.description: Price presented in whole numbers in the lowest denomination, commonly cents. For example 10.00€ would be 1000.

delivery.description: The delivery method of the order.

status.description:
An delivery progresses through a life cycle that consists of different states:

- `estimated`: The time to delivery is estimated by Wolt.
- `assigned`: The delivery is assigned to and accepted by a courier on Wolt.
- `courier_at_venue`: Courier has arrived at the venue to pick up the order.
- `picked_up`: The order has been picked up by courier and is on its way to the consumer.
- `courier_at_delivery_location`: Courier has arrived at the delivery location with the order.
- `delivered`: Courier has completed the delivery.

type.description:
Type of delivery.

- `takeaway`: An order with this item can be picked up by the consumer from the restaurant or store.
- `homedelivery`: An order with this item can be delivered by a Wolt courier.
- `eatin`: The order can be eaten in the restaurant. This feature has been deprecated at Wolt, so while this delivery method will appear in the menu, it is not supported for consumers.

time.description: The date and time (ISO 8601 format) when the order was delivered to the consumer.

self_delivery.description: Indicates whether the order is a self delivery or a Wolt delivery order. Currently the order submitter only supports Wolt delivery orders, so this field will always remain as `false`.

items.description: Items included in the order.

options.description: Options associated with the item in the order.

price.description: Price of the option.

pos_id.description:
Unique identifier for the option in the venue's POS system.

Wolt's menu editor allows storing point of sale (POS) ID. It will be returned as a part of order data to easily map it from Wolt's format to your system.

value_pos_id.description:
Unique identifier for the option value in the venue's POS system.

Wolt's menu editor allows storing point of sale (POS) ID. It will be returned as a part of order data to easily map it from Wolt's format to your system.

name.description: Name of the category as it appears appears in the menu.

row_number.description:
Position of the item in the order.

This is relevant only for retail and is used for item identification purposes.

substitution_settings.description:
Consumer's substitution preferences for the item.

This is relevant only for retail.

is_allowed.description: Whether the item consumer selected can be substituted with a similar item of the same or lower price.

total_price.description: Total price of the item with options and without delivery fees.

unit_price.description: Unit price of the item. Rounded down and calculated with `total_price / count`.

base_price.description: Price of the item without options and delivery fees.

weight_details.description:
Weight details of a weight based item.

This is relevant only for retail.

weight_in_grams.description: Weight of the item in grams.

requested_amount.description:
Quantity of the item requested. Used when the item is priced by weight and sold by piece.

For example: two pieces of watermelon, each piece weighs approximately what is set in `weight_in_grams`.

extra_weight_percentage.description:
Additional percentage of weight allowed when the item is being weighed by the picker in the store.

For example if the initially ordered weight is 500g and the extra weight percentage is 10%, then an additional 10% (550 grams) can be added. Any weight exceeding this cannot be charged to the consumer.

sku.description:
Unique identifier for the item in the venue's enterprise resource planning (ERP) system.

Wolt's menu editor allows setting a stock keeping unit (sku) for the item. It will be returned as a part of order data to easily map it from Wolt's format to your system.

gtin.description:
Unique identifier for the item in the venue's enterprise resource planning (ERP) system.

Wolt's menu editor allows setting a global trade item number (gtin) for the item. It will be returned as a part of order data to easily map it from Wolt's format to your system.

pos_id.description:
Unique identifier for the item in the venue's POS system.

Wolt's menu editor allows setting a point of sale (POS) ID for the item. It will be returned as a part of order data to easily map it from Wolt's format to your system.

item_type.description:
Type of the item. Item's type is linked to the type of venue.

 Restaurant items by default use `order-item` type, while retail stores use `order-retail-item`.

created_at.description: The date and time (ISO 8601 format) when the order was received by Wolt's system.

consumer_comment.description:
Comment added to the order by consumer.

When making an order using Wolt app, a consumer can leave a message to the restaurant. For example to inform the kitchen about dietary restrictions.

pickup_eta.description: The date and time (ISO 8601 format) when the courier is expected to pick up the order.

attribution_id.description:
Unique identifier for the attribution.

This is used to track consumer "source" if the consumer is coming to Wolt from a merchant's website or app. Merchants can create a unique attribution IDs for a campaign or source and pass it to Wolt. This ID is carried through the order flow and reflected in the order.

type.description:
An order can be of two different types.

- `instant`: When an order is to be fulfilled instantly.
- `preorder`: When a consumer schedules an order.

preorder_time.description: The date and time (ISO 8601 format) when the pre-order should be delivered.

pre_order_status.description:
An pre-order progresses through a life cycle that consists of different states:

- `waiting`: The pre-order is waiting to be confirmed by the venue.
- `confirmed`: The pre-order was seen by the venue and has been confirmed.

consumer_name.description:
Name of the consumer who made the order.

If a self-delivery venue has full name setting enabled they will receive the full name of the consumer, otherwise the name will include only first name and first letter of last name.

consumer_phone_number.description:
Phone number of the consumer who made the order.

Consumer phone number is not shared unless absolutely necessary. This is toggled on only for select markets where the phone number is available on the Wolt Merchant app or for self-delivery venues. The field is null in all other cases.

order_number.description: A human readable order number that is unique only for open orders. Order numbers can repeat and are not unique for a venue.

order_status.description:
Status of the order. An order progresses through a life cycle that consists of different states:

- `received`: The order was fetched by the Wolt Merchant app and/or acknowledged by venue staff on the app.
- `fetched`: The order was fetched in the Wolt Merchant app.
- `acknowledged`: The order was interacted by venue staff on the Wolt Merchant app.
- `production`: Preparation of the order has started.
- `ready`: The order has been prepared and is awaiting delivery.
- `delivered`: The order has been delivered to the consumer.
- `rejected`: The venue or Wolt's system rejected the order.
- `refunded`: Wolt has processed a refund for the order.

modified_at.description:
The date and time (ISO 8601 format) when the order was last modified.

Orders move through a life cycle and can change the order status. This change is also considered a modification, so the date and time could be the time when a purchase changed its status from `acknowledged` to `production`.

company_tax_id.description:
Unique identifier for company tax.

In some markets, consumers are allowed to bill their company for the purchase. In these situations they input the company's tax ID and this information is passed on for accounting purposes.
